name: Adjective in -Ful

1.definition: Characterizes something as having or displaying the substance or property associated with the base.

projection.target: The output is adjectival and can modify reply. Noun formations like cupful have a separate measure interpretation and can take plural morphology.
projection.evidence: See the cited discussion and the constructed illustration.

curious.title: Adjectives ending in -ful
curious.summary: Adding -ful to a noun gives an adjective saying something has or displays what the noun names.
curious.body:
A thoughtful reply is one that shows thought. The -ful adjective describes something as having or displaying the substance or property associated with the base word.

The base is typically a noun. Colour gives colourful, a word for something that has colour or displays it. A related ending, -less, works in the opposite direction.
curious.try: Add -ful to a noun such as joy or help. What does the new word say about something?

teacher.summary: Helps explain -ful adjectives as formed from a base meaning having or displaying that property.
teacher.explain: An adjective in -ful characterizes something as having or displaying the substance or property associated with the base, typically a noun. In The chair gave a thoughtful reply, thoughtful describes a reply that displays thought. This dictionary treats it as a specialization of the adjective construction and relates it to the privative -less pattern, which marks lack.
watch_for: A learner might read thoughtful as describing the chair, when it describes the reply.
A learner might confuse -ful with its related privative pattern -less, which marks the opposite idea.
teacher.activity: Students list nouns (care, joy, help), add -ful, and write a sentence with each new adjective. A partner restates it as has or shows the noun.

child.hook: What word describes a reply that shows thought?
child.explain: Add -ful to a word like thought and you get a word saying someone has it or shows it. A thoughtful reply shows thought. A colourful kite has colour.
child.play: Try adding -ful to joy, help and care. Use each new word in a short sentence.

cite: Reynolds, Brett, ed. 2026. "Adjective in -Ful." English Constructionary. https://brettreynolds.ca/constructionary/linguist/endowed-ful-001/ (snapshot 2026-11-19, 5c11b28).
